about: Shared record cases every client runs on each path it has (internal/clientcases). Each case
breaks one rule and carries its correct own digest (sealed again), beside an accepted twin
that breaks none, so the rule it names is the only check that can refuse it. The three
unanswered cases are written by hand (finding release-76: a lost call's record stating a result digest
beside its code, or a code outside the closed set, passed two clients' attach checks);
their record digests were computed by record/testdata/record_v6.py's digest, the
independent implementation written from docs/run-records.md, and Go's runner checks them.
The files-answer cases (finding session-files-1: a files result's second answer, or an answer
of another operation or beside an error, passed the Python and TypeScript checks) carry a
request and the response a daemon sent, its record inside; their digests come from the same
record_v6.py functions, and Go's runner recomputes each it can decode. On the answer path the
response is checked against the request sent, on lost-answer against its own record, as an
attach's lost answer is, which cannot check the operation (docs/run-records.md, "A file call's answer").
The cases of finding session-files-20 are sealed over a twin of typed values (a flag true, a
number 420), then one field is given a JSON type the protocol's JSON form does not allow ("false",
1, 420.5, true), which every client must refuse as malformed, never hash by its truthiness or hand
its caller; their accepted twin gives the integers in proto3 JSON's other form.
expect: the verdict on each path, accept or <outcome>/<check>. An attach refuses a lost
record that does not check as a broken chain, so attach-lost states chain where the
record paths state mismatch. Ids are never reused: a retired case's id moves to retired.

cases.breaks: nothing: the unchanged twin, an unanswered call's record stating the code unavailable and no result digest, at the checkpoint's next call
the record states a result digest beside its unanswered code (both, not exactly one), sealed again
the record's unanswered text is not one of the closed set of Connect codes, sealed again
nothing: the unchanged twin, a stat call answered with its stat
nothing: a stat call answered with an error and its errno, and no answer
nothing: a stat call whose deadline passed, with no error and no answer
nothing: a read_many answer, one item read and one item's error with no bytes
the result holds a stat answer and a read answer of other bytes, and the record's result digest covers the stat alone (finding session-files-1)
a stat call answered with a read answer, sealed over that answer; an attach has the record's request digest and not the request, so it cannot tell
a completed call states an error and still carries an answer
a completed call states no error and carries no answer
a completed call states no error, its answer, and an errno name
a call whose deadline passed carries an answer
a call whose helper ended without an answer states an error
the outcome is setup_failed, which no file call has
the outcome is unspecified
a read_many item states an error and still carries bytes
a read_many item states no error and an errno name

a listing page's more is the string "false", where the record covers more true: a client that hashes the flag by its truthiness verifies it and hands its caller the string, which a reader of more === true takes for the last page (finding session-files-20)
a read_many answer's more is the number 1, where the record covers more true: a flag is a JSON boolean (finding session-files-20)
a stat answer's mode is 420.5, where the record covers 420: an integer field is a whole number (finding session-files-20)
a stat answer's size is true, where the record covers 1: an integer field is a number or a decimal string (finding session-files-20)

nothing: the twin with its integers in the other form proto3 JSON allows (mode as the decimal string "420", a size as a JSON number), which every client reads as the same values the record covers (finding session-files-20: a client must decode them, not only hash them)

a stat answer is the number 0, where the record covers an empty stat answer: an answer of the oneof is a JSON object (Go's protojson refuses it; the TypeScript client read it as an answer and decoded none)

a make_dir answer is the number 0, where the record covers an empty make_dir answer: an answer of the oneof is a JSON object, an empty one included (the Python client took any value but null as the answer)
a remove answer is the string "x", where the record covers an empty remove answer: an answer of the oneof is a JSON object (the Python client took any value but null as the answer)
an answered error's errno name is the number 5, where the record covers the string "5": a string field is a JSON string
a listing's entry is the number 1, where the record covers one empty entry: each entry is a JSON object
